Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline has the records needed to pay every affected member directly. We propose a settlement that delivers meaningful relief without a claims process. Our fee request remains subject to court approval, and any reduction would benefit the class rather than revert to Brightline.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Thank you for the proposal. We have no counterproposal at this time.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We propose a $32 million class fund with automatic payments to all identifiable members. Fees and expenses would be capped at $5 million, subject to court approval; any amount not awarded would go to the class. Brightline need not agree to refrain from opposing the fee request. This structure prioritizes direct class recovery and can be presented transparently to the court.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: defense
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet: a $32 million class fund with automatic distribution, plus up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses; no clear-sailing provision, and any unawarded fees go to the class.

Ostrander Bell LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Ostrander Bell LLP.message: We propose a $36 million class fund, distributed automatically to the approximately 400,000 identifiable members, plus $7 million in court-approved attorneys’ fees and expenses. Any fee amount the court does not award would go to the class. We are not requesting a clear-sailing provision. This structure delivers direct relief without a claims barrier and keeps the fee request fully subject to judicial review.

Ostrander Bell LLP.speaker: defense
Ostrander Bell LLP.message: Thank you for the proposal. We have no counterproposal at this time.

Whitcombe Reyes offers the lowest total cash outlay ($37 million), within the $40 million authorization. Automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and directing any fee reduction to the class support court approval. Accepting now secures those terms without risking a less favorable outcome.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: On behalf of the proposed class, Whitcombe Reyes LLP made one settlement proposal: a $32 million class fund distributed automatically to identifiable members, plus up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses. The proposal contained no clear-sailing provision and directed any fees not awarded to the class. Brightline accepted that proposal in the first round without a counteroffer. Class relief and fees were proposed together; they were not negotiated sequentially. The complete negotiation transcript is being filed with the preliminary-approval motion. The settlement remains subject to court approval, including approval of any fee award.
